seoTitle: Declared Language vs Page Text Checker
metaDescription: Guess the language of a text from script and common words, then compare it with your lang or hreflang code and flag a mismatch.
intro: Checks whether the language your markup declares matches what the text really is.
why:
A page marked lang="nl" that is mostly German, or a translated page that was never translated, is a common hreflang failure. Paste the text and the declared code; the tool detects the script and the most frequent function words and tells you whether they match.

It is a simple heuristic: 11 Latin-script languages by common words, plus script detection for CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew, Greek, Devanagari and Thai. It cannot separate languages that share a script and it ignores the region part. Google does not use hreflang or lang to detect language and works it out itself.
howTo: Paste a paragraph of the page text.
Enter the declared code, for example de-AT.
Read the detected languages with their shares.

faq.q: How much text does it need?
faq.a: At least a few sentences. Very short text is flagged as unreliable.
English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Swedish, Polish, Turkish, Indonesian, plus scripts.
The AI Language Identifier on this site covers 176 languages in the browser.
